text:
samir: heads up — starting the RBAC split for private control plane v2 now. superuser role is being split into admin + support-editor. rolling to 3 tenants first. any known gotchas with Dedicated or on‑prem agents?

lucy: :eyes: saw a couple of failures in audit logs during the canary. agents in tenant-beta lost KMS decrypt on background sync job. logs show 403 from KMS.

jordan: what does the principal look like in the log? service account or node?

lucy: service-account:redwood-onprem-agent@tenant-beta.svc — error: PermissionDenied. stack trace below (trimmed):
```
rpc failed: googleapis.com/kms/v1/projects/.../cryptoKeys/rdw-key: PERMISSION_DENIED
caller=onprem-sync.go:214
```

mike: that usually means the KMS key binding uses a conditional with network/location or a role that references the old superuser group. when we split roles the binding may still reference group:roles/superuser instead of group:roles/admin.

samir: ah — we updated RBAC in control plane but forgot to reconcile cloud key bindings. is this the KMS key policy attached to tenant-beta?

lucy: yes. current binding snippet from GCP IAM: `members: - group:internal-superusers@redwood.com role:roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` — the group no longer gets that role after split.

jordan: quick mitigation: add the new admin group to the binding temporarily or grant the service account directly. which is less invasive?

mike: safer to update the binding to include new group:admin@redwood.com and add a comment / audit entry. direct service-account perms create sprawl.

samir: agree. lifecycle: 1) add new group to KMS binding 2) run canary sync 3) reconcile policy as part of RBAC PR to avoid drift. who can patch the binding?

lucy: I can open a request with infra. putting a Y/N on doing the group-add now (low-risk rollback possible). :thumbsup: for me.

samir: go for it. also — we need to update our audit alerting rule. security-bot, please flag any KMS PERMISSION_DENIED events tied to onprem agents during rollout.

security-bot: acknowledged. creating alert rule `kms-decrypt-fail-onprem-rollout` scoped to tenant tags and service-account patterns.

jordan: after we patch the binding, let's run the playbook: `scripts/onprem/check-kms-bindings.sh tenant-beta` and validate `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` output.

mike: note for the postmortem — this was a policy drift issue where control plane role sync updated user/group RBAC but external resource bindings (KMS) were not part of the same transaction. we should add a preflight check to the RBAC rollout tool that validates external role dependencies.

samir: good call. I'll file a follow-up ticket (SEC-1248) to add the preflight hook and a runbook entry. thanks team — keep updates in this thread.

lucy: bind applied, rerunning canary now. will report back in ~10m. :rotating_light:

lucy: canary success — decrypts resumed, no new 403s in the last 15m. closing the immediate outage. leaving the alert open for 24h.

samir: great work. assign SEC-1248 to me and add docs to the RBAC playbook. also add a one‑line note in the tenant rollout checklist: `reconcile external IAM bindings (KMS, S3 key policies)`.

mike: thanks — marking this as mitigated. :white_check_mark:
